## Interpretation -> modeling decisions (Phase 1 conclusions)
1. Blend weight prior w ~= 0.5 (std betas 0.305 pts / 0.312 xG_all for next-season pts). xg_pct_all
   slightly out-predicts xg_pct_5v5_adj one season ahead (0.549 vs 0.523) - special teams are real
   skill; use all-situations xG, keep 5v5 as robustness check.
2. Two-ahead shrinkage: use directly-estimated 2-lag slope (~0.38 in pts% space; ~0.75x the 1-lag),
   NOT phi^2 (0.26) - quality has a persistent component beyond AR(1).
3. sh%/sv% YoY r ~= 0.006 -> PDO is luck; regression via MOV-Elo + xG blend handles it.
4. OT submodel: p(reach OT) ~= 0.225 (3v3 era), skill slope compressed to ~0.40 of regulation,
   home edge in OT ~= 51%; SO share of past-regulation games ~= 0.34.
5. HFA: calibrate to recent home win% ~= 53.5-54% (declining era).
6. Calibration targets: mean pts/82 ~= 91.3 (translates to ~93.5-94/84g); recent sd(pts/82) ~= 15-17
   (2021/2022 unbalanced-schedule seasons inflate; weigh 2023-2026).
7. Expansion rating prior irrelevant for 2027-28 (32 teams confirmed); backtest uses 1470 for
   VGK/SEA entries with a note (VGK lesson: expansion priors are high-variance).

PARAMS: K=6, H=35, phi_s=0.7, w=0.6 (Elo) / 0.4 (xG_all), phi1=0.85, phi2=0.75, sigma1=30, sigma2=40 Elo.

- 2025-26 was a hard season for everyone (uniform beat all skill models; spearman 0.14) - parity year;
  relevant caveat for 2027-28: league spread is compressing.
